TUTORIAL1.trigger: Tutorial Hints option is on and, on the very first turn (Discoverer level), the player's ship carrying a pioneer and soldier is selected on the high seas; shown once.
TUTORIAL1.inputs: Active unit and its type/owner, turn counter (turn 0), difficulty (Discoverer), the per-hint shown bit, and whether the ship is on screen.
TUTORIAL1.outputs: Pops a hint box explaining to sail west (left arrow) to find land or east (right arrow) to return to port, then sets the hint's shown bit so it never repeats.

TUTORIAL2.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: shown when the ship has found uncharted land and the player should disembark.
TUTORIAL2.inputs: Active ship unit position relative to land; tutorial shown-bit.
TUTORIAL2.outputs: Hint box telling the player to move the ship toward land and choose Make Landfall to put colonists ashore.

TUTORIAL3.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a pioneer is on a tile whose surroundings have abundant resources and at least ~5 nearby land tiles, suggesting a first colony site; shown once.
TUTORIAL3.inputs: Active unit position, 8/9-neighbour terrain scan (land/colony counts via terrain-id and colony-index lookups), the named resource of the area; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL3.outputs: Hint box saying the abundance here makes a good first-colony spot and to press 'B' to build; sets the shown bit.

TUTORIAL4.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: the player opens the Colony Screen for the very first time (first-visit block in the colony dialog).
TUTORIAL4.inputs: Active colony, its current worker and what it produces, an empty surrounding ring tile; shown-bit on the colony-screen-seen flag.
TUTORIAL4.outputs: Hint box explaining the Colony Screen and Jobs Menu (change a colonist's job, drag him to a tile/building, or to the fence to remove him); sets the seen bit.

TUTORIAL5.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: colonists are waiting on the docks in the home Europe port ready to join a colony, prompting the player to send a ship.
TUTORIAL5.inputs: Europe-port immigrant queue (which specialists are on the docks), the home port name; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL5.outputs: Hint box noting colonists are ready on the docks in Europe and a ship sent there will bring them to the New World.

TUTORIAL6.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a colony has accumulated a sellable cargo, prompting the player to ship it to Europe for profit.
TUTORIAL6.inputs: Colony stored-cargo amount and type, the colony name and the home Europe port name; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL6.outputs: Hint box telling the player to move a ship into the colony, pick up the cargo, and sell it in Europe.

TUTORIAL7.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a colony is growing rapidly and is unprotected, suggesting the player build a Stockade.
TUTORIAL7.outputs: Hint box explaining the build chain (Lumberjack chops lumber, Carpenter makes buildings, then click the Hammer button to choose what to build) and to consider a Stockade.

TUTORIAL8.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a colonist with no specialty profession stands near a friendly native village that could teach a skill.
TUTORIAL8.inputs: Active unit type/profession (no specialty), terrain/feature under and around the unit (native village within range); shown-bit.
TUTORIAL8.outputs: Hint box suggesting moving the unspecialized colonist into the friendly native village so the natives may teach him a skill.

TUTORIAL9.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a pioneer is on a tile that is a good place for a road (resource terrain band).
TUTORIAL9.inputs: Active pioneer position, neighbour terrain band scan; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL9.outputs: Hint box explaining roads (press 'R'); roads boost fur/lumber/ore/silver here and speed unit movement.

TUTORIAL10.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a pioneer is on a tile that is a good place to plow or clear (forest/terrain band, >=2 forest neighbours).
TUTORIAL10.inputs: Active pioneer position, 8-neighbour forest/terrain-band count; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL10.outputs: Hint box explaining plowing (press 'P'): plowing raises food/tobacco/cotton/sugar by one, and plowing a forest clears it for agriculture.

TUTORIAL11.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: early game (turn < 20), the player's ship is selected, explaining what ships are for; shown once.
TUTORIAL11.inputs: Active unit type/cargo, turn counter, the ship's type name and home port; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL11.outputs: Hint box describing the ship's uses (explore, carry cargo home, bring immigrants) and controls (arrow keys, 'G' to send to a port).

TUTORIAL12.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: the player opens the colony screen of a port colony where a ship is waiting for cargo (first-visit block B with a ship-type unit present).
TUTORIAL12.inputs: Active colony, presence of a ship-type defender (unit type in the ship band) at the colony, the colony name; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL12.outputs: Hint box explaining how to drag warehouse cargo into the ship's holds, return to the map (ESC), then send the ship to Europe with 'G'.

TUTORIAL13.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: early game (turn < 20), the player's pioneers (type 2) have just arrived in the New World and have no feature yet; shown once.
TUTORIAL13.inputs: Active unit type (pioneers), turn counter, whether the tile has a feature; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL13.outputs: Hint box advising to find a coastal site with food/resources for the first colony, noting pioneers carry 100 Tools for clearing/plowing/roads.

TUTORIAL14.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: early game (turn < 20), the player's soldiers (type 1) have arrived with no feature yet; shown once.
TUTORIAL14.inputs: Active unit type (soldiers), turn counter, tile feature flag; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL14.outputs: Hint box explaining soldiers attack and defend, carry 50 Muskets, and become stronger when equipped with Horses.

TUTORIAL15.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: new colonists have arrived in a colony (turn < 40), prompting the player to assign them.
TUTORIAL15.inputs: Active unit type (colonist, type 0), turn counter, the destination colony record/name; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL15.outputs: Hint box telling the player to click the colony and drag the new colonists from the fence into a field or building.

TUTORIAL19.trigger: Tutorial Hints on: a colonist of type 0 is on/near specific terrain (converts context), explaining native Converts; shown once.
TUTORIAL19.inputs: Active unit type and the terrain under it; shown-bit.
TUTORIAL19.outputs: Hint box explaining Converts (natives who join your colonies): they cannot be educated but are better at farming, planting, fishing, and mining.

ARMOPTIONS.trigger: Player clicks a unit on the European dock/harbor to open its options menu.
ARMOPTIONS.inputs: Selected unit's type, the costs to arm/equip with Muskets, Tools, or Horses (and the sale credits), and whether it can be blessed as a missionary.
ARMOPTIONS.outputs: Shows the dock-options menu: board/skip next ship, move to front of dock, arm/sell Muskets, equip/sell Tools, equip/sell Horses, bless/cancel Missionary status, or no changes.

REALLYBUY.trigger: Player confirms a purchase action that costs gold (e.g. buying a recruit, specialist, or item) and the game asks for final confirmation.
REALLYBUY.inputs: The item/thing being purchased and its gold cost.
REALLYBUY.outputs: Yes/No confirmation prompt 'Purchase X for $N?'; on Yes the purchase proceeds and gold is deducted.

TRIBUTE.trigger: During a European-power diplomacy meeting, the other (e.g. Catholic) power offers to overlook your colonies in exchange for a gold 'donation'.
TRIBUTE.inputs: The demanding power's sponsor name, the natives/region cited, your colony location, and the demanded donation amount in gold; your treasury.
TRIBUTE.outputs: Presents the demand: refuse ('Not a penny for those heretic swine') or pay the donation; paying transfers the gold and avoids hostility.

MULTI.trigger: Multiplayer start is selected (via the COLONIZE_MULTI environment variable or a command-line/menu option), prompting selection of human-controlled powers.
MULTI.inputs: The COLONIZE_MULTI env var (compared against 'MULTI'), command-line argv option markers; the active-power roster.
MULTI.outputs: Shows the 'Multiplayer Start Selected' screen and lets the player pick which European powers are controlled by human players.

SAVEGAME.trigger: Player chooses Save Game from the menu, opening the save-slot picker.
SAVEGAME.inputs: The current game state and the available save slots (filenames built as COLONY<slot>.SAV); the save command is gated by the SAVEGAME message key.
SAVEGAME.outputs: Shows the 'Select Save Slot' dialog; on a chosen slot it invokes the save driver to write the COLONIZE-magic save file, then reports success (SAVEGOOD) or an error (SAVEERROR).

LOADGAME.trigger: Player chooses Load Game from the menu, opening the load-slot picker.
LOADGAME.inputs: Available save files in the slots; the load command is gated by the LOADGAME message key; each file's COLONIZE magic, version, and map size are validated.
LOADGAME.outputs: Shows the 'Select Game To Load' dialog; on a chosen slot it runs the load driver and maps the result to a message (LOADGOOD / LOADNOT / LOADOLD / LOADSIZE / LOADERROR).

NATION0A.trigger: New-game initialization draws the leader/nation intro panel after the starting European power is chosen (randomly picked 0-3 unless multiplayer).
NATION0A.inputs: The randomly chosen nation index (England/France/Spain/Netherlands), the leader-name string, and the chosen nation's history/description text section.
NATION0A.outputs: Composes the intro panel (WOODPANL background + LEADERNAME prompt + the NATION0A-family nation description text) and zero-initializes the per-power PowerRecord and AIPersonality tables.

MAPTOLOAD.trigger: Player starts a game in AMERICA and chooses 'Map Editor' (custom map), opening the .MP map-file picker.
MAPTOLOAD.inputs: The list of available '*.MP' map files in the save/data directory; menu keys OPENMENU/BEGINMENU/AMERICA drive the surrounding screen.
MAPTOLOAD.outputs: Shows the 'Select Map File to Load' header and file list; the chosen .MP map name is recorded (replacing the default AMER2.MP) and loaded.

HAVETREATY.trigger: The active unit tries to build a colony or act on a tile adjacent to a native settlement of a tribe with whom you have a peace treaty.
HAVETREATY.inputs: The active unit, an 8-neighbour scan for an adjacent native settlement owned by a matching tribe, the tribe identity.
HAVETREATY.outputs: Warns 'We have signed a peace treaty with the {tribe}' and offers Cancel Action or Break Treaty; breaking the treaty flags the settlement and claims the tile.

TRADENONE.trigger: Player tries to assign a unit to a trade route but no trade routes have been defined yet.
TRADENONE.outputs: Shows 'You have not yet defined any trade routes.' and aborts the assignment.

TRADESELECT.trigger: Player assigns a unit to a trade route and at least one route exists, opening the route picker.
TRADESELECT.inputs: The active unit, its type (ship vs land determines route kind), and the list of defined trade routes.
TRADESELECT.outputs: Shows 'Select a trade route:'; on a pick the unit is assigned to that route and put into trade-route order.

BUYME0.trigger: Player asks to rush/complete a colony's current build project but cannot afford it (information-only variant, no choices).
BUYME0.inputs: The current build item's name, the gold cost to complete it, and the treasury balance.
BUYME0.outputs: Displays 'Cost to complete X: $N. Treasury: $M.' as an informational message (no buy option offered because funds are insufficient).

BUYME1.trigger: Player asks to rush/complete a colony's current build project and can afford it (choice variant).
BUYME1.inputs: The current build item's name, the gold cost to complete it, and the treasury balance.
BUYME1.outputs: Shows 'Cost to complete X: $N. Treasury: $M.' with options Never mind / Complete it; choosing Complete spends the gold and finishes the build.

DEPLETION.trigger: During colony turn processing, a worked resource tile in the colony's surrounding ring (a mine/ore site) becomes depleted.
DEPLETION.inputs: Sweep of the colony's 8 surrounding cells, each cell's terrain class (resource-bearing 6/7) and feature; the colony name.
DEPLETION.outputs: Changes the depleted map tile and shows 'Mine depleted near {colony}.'

CANESUGAR.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored sugar so its distillers cannot work.
CANESUGAR.inputs: The colony's sugar stock (zero) and the colony name.
CANESUGAR.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of sugar... Our distillers cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

COTTON.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored cotton so its weavers cannot work.
COTTON.inputs: The colony's cotton stock (zero) and the colony name.
COTTON.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of cotton... Our weavers cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

FURS.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored furs so its fur traders cannot work.
FURS.inputs: The colony's furs stock (zero) and the colony name.
FURS.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of furs... Our fur traders cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

LUMBER.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored lumber so its carpenters cannot work.
LUMBER.inputs: The colony's lumber stock (zero) and the colony name.
LUMBER.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of lumber... Our carpenters cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

NEEDTOOLS.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony's build project needs more tools than are available to finish.
NEEDTOOLS.inputs: The colony name, the building under construction, the tools required for completion, and the tools currently available.
NEEDTOOLS.outputs: Shows '{building} under construction in {colony} requires {N} tools for completion. Only {M} tools are currently available.'

TOBACCO.trigger: During colony turn processing, a colony runs out of stored tobacco so its tobacconists cannot work.
TOBACCO.inputs: The colony's tobacco stock (zero) and the colony name.
TOBACCO.outputs: Shows '{colony} has run out of tobacco... Our tobacconists cannot continue their work until a new supply is found.'

REFIT.trigger: A damaged ship that had returned to a colony/Europe for repairs finishes repairing.
REFIT.inputs: The ship's name and the port/colony where it was repaired.
REFIT.outputs: Shows '{ship} has completed its repairs in {port}.'

KISSSORRY.trigger: Player agrees to pay back-taxes to lift a Parliamentary boycott (after the KISSUP prompt) but does not have enough gold.
KISSSORRY.inputs: The player's available gold (less than the back-tax amount demanded).
KISSSORRY.outputs: Shows 'Unfortunately, we only have $N available.' and the boycott is not lifted.

ORDINAL.trigger: Not a dialog: an ordinal-word lookup table (first, second, third, ... thirtieth) used to compose other messages.
ORDINAL.inputs: A 1-based index into the ordinal list.
ORDINAL.outputs: Returns the ordinal word for that index (e.g. for naming the Nth founding father, Nth wife, etc.) to be inserted into another message.

CANCELPEACE.trigger: A peace treaty between two powers is cancelled (e.g. via the right-click give-command / declare-war handler, or when a power breaks a treaty).
CANCELPEACE.inputs: The two power/tribe names whose treaty is ending.
CANCELPEACE.outputs: Announces '{power} cancel peace treaty with {power}.' and sets the two parties' relations to no-treaty/war.
CANCELPEACE.func: func_03ECF0 (ai_eval_unit / declare-war handler, ported to ai/unit_orders.c + diplomacy/relations.c)

BADHAGGLE0.trigger: While trading goods with a native village, the player haggles too long and the natives lose patience with this offer.
BADHAGGLE0.inputs: The cargo being offered to the natives.
BADHAGGLE0.outputs: Shows 'Our patience with your haggling is exhausted. We no longer want your worthless {cargo}...' and ends this trade.

BADHAGGLE1.trigger: Player returns to trade the same cargo the natives already refused after over-haggling.
BADHAGGLE1.outputs: Shows 'We have already told you that we no longer want your {cargo}. Come back when you have something else.'

BRING.trigger: After a native trade interaction, the village hints at what goods it wants for next time.
BRING.inputs: The two/three cargo types the village is in need of.
BRING.outputs: Shows 'We are in need of {A} and {B}. Perhaps you will bring some next time... Even {C} would be of some value.'

NOTENOUGH.trigger: During a native trade the player promises a buy/payment larger than their treasury can back.
NOTENOUGH.outputs: Shows 'Sadly, your treasury ($N) is not large enough to back your promise.' and the deal falls through.

LEARNSTAY.trigger: An unskilled colonist (Young One) visits a native village willing to teach him a master profession.
LEARNSTAY.inputs: The tribe and the master profession they can teach.
LEARNSTAY.outputs: Offers 'we {tribe} will show you how to become a master {profession}' with choices to become the master now or decline.

EXTORTNO.trigger: A scout/unit demands tribute (extortion) from a native village but the village refuses outright.
EXTORTNO.inputs: The player's leader title and the tribe identity.
EXTORTNO.outputs: Shows the refusal 'You must think us very foolish indeed... The {tribe} will not be taken in by your tricks and treachery.'

EXTORTPOOR.trigger: A unit extorts a native village that has no goods worth giving.
EXTORTPOOR.inputs: The player's leader title and the tribe identity.
EXTORTPOOR.outputs: Shows 'the humble and peaceloving {tribe} have no gifts worthy of your magnificence. We pray that you will be merciful and spare us.'

EXTORTSTUFF.trigger: A unit successfully extorts goods from an intimidated native village.
EXTORTSTUFF.inputs: The player's leader title, the tribe, the goods amount/type extorted, and the destination colony.
EXTORTSTUFF.outputs: Shows the village conceding to deliver {N} {goods} to {colony} to be spared, and the goods are transferred.

ALREADYSMITE.trigger: Player asks a European power (in diplomacy) to attack a native tribe they are already at war with.
ALREADYSMITE.inputs: The named tribe and the other power's existing war state against it.
ALREADYSMITE.outputs: Shows 'We are already at war with the worthless {tribe}.'

NOCONTACT.trigger: Player asks a power to act against a tribe with whom that power has had no contact.
NOCONTACT.inputs: The named tribe and the asked power's contact state.
NOCONTACT.outputs: Shows 'We have no contact with the {tribe}.'

UNFORTUNATE.trigger: Player agrees to pay a power (e.g. to smite a tribe or move forces) but lacks the gold to cover the promise.
UNFORTUNATE.inputs: The player's treasury balance versus the promised amount.
UNFORTUNATE.outputs: Shows 'Unfortunately, your treasury is insufficient to match your extravagant promises.' and the deal is void.

SIGNTREATY.trigger: Two powers/tribes conclude a peace treaty (announcement).
SIGNTREATY.outputs: Announces 'The {A} and {B} have signed a peace treaty.'

GIFTS.trigger: During a European-power diplomacy meeting the other power offers a gift of gold for continued forbearance.
GIFTS.outputs: Shows 'We present you with a gift of $N in exchange for your continued forbearance.' and credits the gold.

PEACEUSA.trigger: In diplomacy with an independent (post-revolution USA) nation, that nation responds to a peace proposal.
PEACEUSA.inputs: The USA nation name and your nation name.
PEACEUSA.outputs: Shows the USA peace response with reply options (Go in peace / withdraw forces first / threat / suggest an alliance).

PROVOKE.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power declares war over your provocations.
PROVOKE.outputs: Shows 'We can no longer tolerate your foul provocations. Prepare for WAR!' and sets the two powers at war.

RID.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power orders you to leave a region/the hemisphere or be driven out.
RID.inputs: The power's sponsor name and the region/colony in question.
RID.outputs: Shows the ultimatum 'we order you to leave {region} immediately. If you do not, we shall drive you into the sea.'

THREATS.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power dismisses your threat.
THREATS.outputs: Shows 'We laugh at your feeble threats.'

WARMANLY.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting you reject a power's offer and it declares war (the assertive 'manly' variant).
WARMANLY.inputs: The power's sponsor name and the region in question.
WARMANLY.outputs: Shows 'You reject our generous offer? Then in the name of {sponsor} we shall wipe you from the face of the New World. Prepare for WAR!'

WITHDRAW.trigger: During a diplomacy meeting the other power agrees to withdraw its forces in the interest of peace.
WITHDRAW.outputs: Shows 'In the interest of peace, we shall withdraw our forces.' and the forces pull back to Europe.

TRADENOWANT.trigger: A wagon train / ship offers goods to a native village that is not interested in that cargo.
TRADENOWANT.inputs: The offered cargo amount and type.
TRADENOWANT.outputs: Shows 'We are not interested in your {N} {cargo}. Come back when you have something better to offer.'

EVASIVE.trigger: In combat, an attacking unit's strike misses and the defender evades it (combat-outcome verb emitted by the land-combat decider).
EVASIVE.inputs: Attacker and defender unit names/owners, the resolved combat roll.

TRADEDELETE.trigger: Player chooses to delete a defined trade route.
TRADEDELETE.inputs: The list of existing trade routes (route count) and the chosen route to delete.
TRADEDELETE.outputs: Shows 'Which trade route should we delete:' then, on confirmation, detaches units assigned to it, compacts the route table, and decrements the route count.

LOSENOCOLONIES.trigger: End-of-turn king check: from the year 1600 onward, the player has zero colonies and is not in the War of Independence.
LOSENOCOLONIES.inputs: The active power's colony count (zero), the current year (>= 1600), the war flag (not at war), the player's leader title and name.
LOSENOCOLONIES.outputs: The King removes the player as Viceroy ('Our efforts in the New World have proven fruitless...'); the score result is zeroed and the game ends in defeat.

SCORE.trigger: End of game: the score/Hall-of-Fame screen is shown and computes the player's rank, which selects a legacy-naming line.
SCORE.inputs: The raw per-power score (population, colonies, founding fathers, gold, bells, etc. - see note), the difficulty factor (Discoverer/Explorer/Conquistador/Governor/Viceroy map to 4/5/6/8/10), and the player/leader name. Rank 0-23 is found via pct = factor*raw_score/100 binned through a quadratic ladder ((k*k)/3 < pct), clamped to 23. The factor math and rank ladder are byte-verified; the raw-score component WEIGHTS live in an overlay routine and are NOT verified (do not trust the reconstructed SCORING.md formula).
SCORE.outputs: Picks one entry from the legacy list (a Fever / Fly / Ivy / Rattlesnake / ...Boulevard / ...Mountains / Republic of... / ...ica) keyed by the computed rank, naming something after the player, and draws the rank title (@SCORE1..@SCORE24) plus the medallion sprite.
SCORE.func: func_03A9C0 (end-of-game SCORE+RANK screen; rank math in scoring/compute.c score_endgame_rank)

VICEROY.trigger: Start of a new game: the opening 'Audience With The King' investiture screen where the monarch dubs the player Viceroy of the New World.
VICEROY.inputs: The chosen nation/country name and the nation index (Netherlands shows the 'Stadtholder' variant @VICEROY2 instead of 'The King').
VICEROY.outputs: Displays the dub-thee-Viceroy address ('For the greater glory of {country}, we dub thee Viceroy of the New World...') in a year-1492 audience panel; on Netherlands an alternate Stadtholder clause is appended.
